pc_new: Detects secrets in images, containers and hosts. Not in repos or IaC files
quote: Prisma Cloud can detect sensitive information that is improperly secured inside images and containers.
notes: Defender checks 424 (image env vars), 425 (private keys in images) and 597 (container env vars). Agentless checks 456 (container image filesystems) and 457 (host filesystems) scan files for secret types such as AWS, Azure and GCP keys, DB connection strings and SaaS tokens. The code repo scan page (continuous-integration/code-repo-scanning) covers package dependency vulnerabilities only. Compute Edition has no Git history or IaC secret scan. Enterprise-era claim was Parity.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md and docs/faqs/general.md list ASPM, including secret scans, as supported on-prem and air-gapped, and docs/integrations/jenkins-secret-scan.md has a cliPath option for air-gapped agents.

pc_new: Flags secrets in container env vars. No ConfigMap or manifest scan
quote: This check detects sensitive information provided in environment variables of container.
notes: Check 597 inspects environment variables of running containers, which can include values injected from a ConfigMap. No Compute page describes scanning ConfigMap objects or Kubernetes manifests. Kubernetes Secrets appear only as a runtime attack technique label in runtime-defense/attack.
ak_onprem_note: The AccuKnox ConfigMap claim rests on a Storylane demo card in docs/how-to/aspm-overview.md with no written guide, so the on-prem status of this specific check cannot be confirmed. docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AI CoPilot for on-prem.

pc_new: Dependency SCA for 5 runtimes in repos via twistcli and Jenkins plugin
quote: Both twistcli and the Jenkins plugin can evaluate package dependencies in your code repositories for vulnerabilities.
notes: Supported runtimes: Go, Java, Node.js, Python, Ruby. Package license details are collected (vulnerability-management/scan-reports). SBOM export is CycloneDX 1.4 (vulnerability-management/exporting-sboms). twistcli coderepo scan runs on Linux, macOS and Windows and sends a bill of materials to Console for evaluation (tools/twistcli-scan-code-repos).
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says on-prem has all features except AI CoPilot, and docs/getting-started/3.5-release.md describes SBOM scans of artifacts built in air-gapped CI.

pc_new: Repo scans check package dependencies only. No source code analysis
quote: Both twistcli and the Jenkins plugin can evaluate package dependencies in your code repositories for vulnerabilities.
notes: Repo scanning in Compute covers dependency vulnerabilities only. Compute Edition includes the CWPP module only (welcome/product-architecture), and its docs have no pages for SAST or code quality rules. Enterprise-era claim was Limited.
ak_onprem_note: docs/support-matrix/sast-support-matrix.md plus docs/resources/deployment.md (all features on-prem except AI CoPilot). SonarQube gates need a reachable SonarQube server, which is an assumption to confirm.

pc_new: twistcli page lists IaC templates, no scan guide [confirm from Prisma Cloud docs]
quote: The twistcli tool is a command-line utility for interacting with Prisma Cloud to scan containers, images, serverless functions, and IaC (Infrastructure-as-Code) templates.
notes: Only this one sentence names IaC templates. The twistcli reference (tools/twistcli) lists these functions: console, defender, hosts, images, intelligence, tas, app-embedded, restore, serverless, support. It has no IaC command, no IaC policy page and no supported template list. The CI section has no IaC step. The sentence may be carried over from the Enterprise Edition page. Verify with Palo Alto Networks before the bank sees this row. Enterprise-era claim was Parity. The only Compute CloudFormation option is the serverless scan flag --cloudformation-template, which feeds function permission analysis and is not IaC scanning.
ak_onprem_note: docs/support-matrix/iac.md plus docs/integrations/jenkins-iac-scan.md, which allows a mirrored scanner image for air-gapped agents.

pc_new: Image CVE scans in CI, 13 registry types and deployed images, with block or fail rules
quote: Vulnerability rules let you specify alert, block, or fail triggers based on severity thresholds.
notes: Strong and mature. twistcli images scan and the Jenkins plugin scan images in CI and can fail the build. Registry scanning covers Nexus, Alibaba, ECR, ACR, Docker Registry v2, GitLab, Google Artifact Registry, GCR, Harbor, IBM Cloud, JFrog Artifactory, OpenShift and Quay, with webhook triggers. Default scan interval is 24 hours and images rescan on change (configure/configure-scan-intervals). Blocking rules make Defender the arbiter of container lifecycle commands. Kubernetes and OpenShift admission control uses OPA (access-control/open-policy-agent). Windows image scanning exists with limits (windows-image-scanning). Agentless scanning of images covers AWS, Azure and GCP.
ak_onprem_note: docs/use-cases/container-scan.md covers CI/CD, registry and in-cluster scans, and docs/how-to/jfrog-container.md says self-hosted JFrog registries are scanned in on-prem and air-gapped setups.

pc_new: No SARIF import. Compute Edition is the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: The Compute docs contain no SARIF page and no import path for third-party code scanner results. Findings are exported as CycloneDX SBOMs and Prisma Cloud scan reports. Enterprise-era claim was Parity.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/sarif-findings.md has no SaaS-only note, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AI CoPilot for on-prem.

pc_new: Jenkins plugin plus twistcli for other CI. No repo-host app integrations
quote: The Jenkins plugin for Prisma Cloud enables you to scan container images, code repositories, and serverless functions for security vulnerabilities and compliance issues within your continuous integration pipeline.
notes: The continuous-integration section documents Jenkins only: Freestyle, Maven, Pipeline and Pipeline on Kubernetes agents, plus policy targeting. The plugin is built for Jenkins on Linux and supports the current and previous two major releases. twistcli runs on Linux, macOS and Windows and can be called from any CI tool by script, but the docs name no GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps or CircleCI plugin. Registry hosts such as GitLab Container Registry are image sources, not repo integrations. Enterprise-era claim was Parity.
ak_onprem_note: docs/support-matrix/cicd-support-matrix.md plus the Jenkins pages that document a cliPath option for air-gapped agents (docs/integrations/jenkins-sast.md). Git hosts must be reachable from worker nodes per docs/getting-started/on-prem-installation-guide.md.

pc_new: No SAST scanner. Compute Edition is the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: The Compute docs contain no SAST page. Repo scanning evaluates package dependencies only (continuous-integration/code-repo-scanning). Enterprise-era claim was Limited, based on ingesting SAST findings from other tools.
ak_onprem_note: SAST runs on-prem per docs/resources/deployment.md, but the opt-in AI triage in docs/getting-started/3.4-release.md needs an Anthropic API key, so it needs outbound access and is not available air-gapped.

pc_new: No DAST scanner. WAAS protects running web apps and APIs
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: The Compute docs contain no DAST page. WAAS (web-application-and-api-security-waas) is runtime protection with API discovery, not an active scanner. Enterprise-era claim was also Not supported.
ak_onprem_note: docs/how-to/dast-scan-types.md has no SaaS-only note, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AI CoPilot for on-prem. Scan targets must be reachable from the on-prem control plane, which is an assumption to confirm.

pc_new: Exports CycloneDX 1.4 for images, hosts and functions. No SBOM import
quote: Prisma Cloud supports exporting SBOM files in the CycloneDX v1.4 standard
notes: Export formats are cyclonedx_json and cyclonedx_xml. Download by twistcli (--SBOM flag) or REST API for images, hosts, VMs, serverless and registry images. Attributes include name, version, purl, license and author for some package types. The Compute docs contain no SBOM upload, SPDX or third-party SBOM import path.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/sbom.md names CycloneDX and SPDX, and docs/getting-started/3.5-release.md describes scanning artifacts in air-gapped CI. docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features on-prem.

pc_new: Scan reports list installed packages, CVEs and licenses for images and hosts
quote: Scan reports have a **Package info** tab, which lists all the packages installed in an image or host.
notes: Package info lists installed and active packages with license details, and Vulnerability Explorer rolls CVEs up by image, host and function. The inventory comes from Prisma scans, not from imported SBOM files. twistcli coderepo scan sends a bill of materials to Console for evaluation against threat data.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/xbom-setup.md plus docs/resources/deployment.md (all features on-prem except AI CoPilot).

param: Continuous CVE Monitoring for SBOM Components
pc_new: Intelligence Stream updates several times a day. Default rescan every 24 hours
quote: The Intelligence Stream (IS) is updated several times per day, and the consoles check continuously for updates.
notes: Default scan interval is 24 hours and images rescan when changes are detected (configure/configure-scan-intervals). Air-gapped Consoles take Intelligence Stream data by twistcli download and upload, or from a central location checked every 24 hours (tools/update-intel-stream-offline). Rescans cover deployed objects, not stored third-party SBOMs.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/vulnerability-database.md says the vulnerability database refreshes every 12 hours from NVD, EPSS and CISA KEV, and docs/faqs/deployment.md says isolated deployments must set up their own pipeline to push those updates.
